s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory illness with fever and shortness of breath
salient_findings: Fever up to 39°C
Anosmia
Shortness of breath
Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography
key_facts: Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
Coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction
Chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia
Normal sinus rhythm with normal frontal QRS axis on ECG

shortlist.label: COVID-19
shortlist.why_kept: Nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction and symptoms of fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath

shortlist.label: Influenza pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Symptoms of fever, shortness of breath, and bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography

shortlist.label: Pneumococcal pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography and coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe symptoms of fever, shortness of breath, and low oxygen saturation

shortlist.label: Mycoplasma pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Symptoms of fever, shortness of breath, and bilateral multifocal pneumonia on chest radiography in a patient with no clear bacterial infection signs

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, combined with the nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction and chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia, are consistent with COVID-19.

rejected.label: Influenza pneumonia
rejected.why: While influenza can cause similar symptoms, the combination of anosmia and the specific laboratory and imaging findings point more strongly towards COVID-19.

rejected.label: Pneumococcal pneumonia
rejected.why: Pneumococcal pneumonia typically presents with more localized findings on chest radiography and does not typically cause anosmia.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal pneumonia
rejected.why: Staphylococcal pneumonia often presents with more severe disease and specific complications such as cavitation or pneumatoceles, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Mycoplasma pneumonia
rejected.why: Mycoplasma pneumonia can cause multifocal pneumonia but typically affects a younger population and does not usually result in such severe hypoxemia as seen in this patient.
